origins: Teasing, rejection, or constant exposure to idealized images can tie lovability to looks. After a few hurtful experiences, “I’m ugly” becomes “I’m unlovable.”
teaches: “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” His love came before our worth was visible to anyone. “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” Love in Scripture is not a reward for beauty. “Love is patient, love is kind.” People who love you see far more than your face.
self_statements: I am too ugly for anyone.
errors: Believing I am either beautiful or unlovable.
Predicting that no one will love me.
Feeling ugly and concluding I am unlovable.
questions: Who loves me, and does it depend on my looks?
What do I love about the people dear to me?
Who taught me that love follows beauty?
What does God’s love for me look like?
What qualities in me are lovable?
What would change if I believed I was loved?
truth: God loved me before I did anything. Love is not a prize for beauty. I am lovable now, and I can receive love from God and from people.
hw_truths: God loved me while I was a sinner.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
log: Each week, note one sign of love you received.
actions: Write ten qualities that are not about looks.
prayer: Father, You loved me before I was lovely. Heal my sense of being unlovable, and let me receive love. Amen.
